data.title: Zero datum positioning and connected section repositioning

epic.spec:
# Zero Datum Positioning and Connected Section Repositioning

## Overview

When a zero datum (GPS reference point) is set on a station, the station should be positioned at those exact coordinates on the map, and all sections connected through station merges should move relative to the zero datum station. Currently, `set_zero_datum` only stores the GPS coordinates but does not reposition the station or connected sections.

## Scope

**In scope:**
- GPS-to-local coordinate conversion (ENU projection)
- Section repositioning via `section_offsets` when datum is set
- Recompute station coordinates from shots with new origin
- Validation for duplicate datum in connected group
- Enhanced undo data to capture section_offsets
- Merge propagates datum repositioning
- Frontend fit-to-bounds after datum set

**Out of scope:**
- Visual preview before repositioning
- GPS coordinate validation against external services
- Export coordinate conversion (GPS output)

## Quick commands

```bash
# Rust tests
cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml

# Type check frontend
pnpm tsc --noEmit

# Run app
./scripts/dev.sh
```

## Approach

### GPS-to-Local Conversion

Implement ENU (East-North-Up) projection using WGS84 ellipsoid:
1. Convert geodetic (lat, lon) to ECEF (x, y, z)
2. Convert ECEF difference to ENU (east, north, up)
3. First datum GPS becomes projection center
4. Local coordinates: East→x (meters), North→y (meters)

WGS84 constants in Rust:
```rust
const WGS84_A: f64 = 6_378_137.0;  // semi-major axis
const WGS84_E2: f64 = 0.00669437999014;  // eccentricity squared
```

### Section Repositioning

Enhance `Project::set_zero_datum()` to:
1. Find all connected sections via `get_connected_section_ids()`
2. Compute current station coordinates via `compute_station_raw_coords()`
3. For first datum: Station becomes (0,0), no offset changes needed
4. For subsequent datums: Compute GPS offset from first datum in meters
5. Calculate offset needed to move station to target position
6. Apply offset to all connected sections via `section_offsets`

### Undo Enhancement

Modify `UndoData::ZeroDatumInfo` to capture:
```rust
pub struct ZeroDatumInfo {
    pub station_ref: StationRef,
    pub previous_gps: Option<GpsCoordinates>,
    pub previous_offsets: HashMap<SectionId, (f64, f64)>,  // NEW
}
```

### Key Files

| File | Changes |
|------|---------|
| `src-tauri/src/models/project.rs` | Enhance set_zero_datum, add GPS conversion |
| `src-tauri/src/core/undo.rs` | Enhance ZeroDatumInfo with offsets |
| `src-tauri/src/models/project.rs` | Merge propagation for datum |
| `src/store/projectStore.ts` | Call triggerFitToBounds after datum |
| `docs/SPEC.md` | Document zero datum behavior |

### Existing Patterns to Follow

- Section offset application: `project.rs:333-443` (`merge_stations`)
- Connected group traversal: `project.rs:202-222` (`get_connected_section_ids`)
- Coordinate computation: `project.rs:596-727` (`compute_station_coordinates`)
- Undo data capture: `undo.rs:72-77` (`UndoData::ZeroDatumInfo`)

## Edge Cases

- First datum removal: Next datum in vector becomes primary (or none)
- First datum on station with existing offset: GPS position overrides offset
- Datum on merged station: Use the section containing the station
- GPS coordinates identical for different groups: Both groups at same position (valid)
- Merge connects to datum group: Merged sections reposition
- Unmerge from datum group: Detached section keeps current position
- Empty section: Valid to set datum (station still exists)

## Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| Performance with large projects | Only recompute affected connected group |
| GPS conversion accuracy | Use proper ENU projection, not approximation |
| Undo state bloat | Only store affected section offsets |
| Merge/datum interaction complexity | Clear precedence: datum controls offset |

## Test Notes

- Test first datum sets station to (0,0)
- Test second datum on different group uses GPS offset
- Test duplicate datum on same group returns error
- Test undo restores previous positions
- Test merge propagates repositioning
- Test unmerge keeps position
- Test fit-to-bounds called after set

## Acceptance

- [ ] Setting zero datum repositions the station to GPS coordinates (as local coords)
- [ ] First zero datum station becomes local (0,0,z)
- [ ] All transitively connected sections reposition relative to the datum
- [ ] Station coordinates recalculated from shot data using datum as origin
- [ ] Second datum's local position computed from GPS offset relative to first datum
- [ ] Error shown when trying to set datum on already-referenced station group
- [ ] Merge propagates datum repositioning to newly connected sections
- [ ] Unmerge keeps detached section at current position
- [ ] Setting datum is fully undoable (restores previous positions)
- [ ] Removing datum keeps positions, only loses GPS reference
- [ ] Map view fits to bounds after datum is set
- [ ] GPS coordinates validated (-90/90 lat, -180/180 lon)
- [ ] Detailed logging of GPS coords, offsets, and affected stations
- [ ] Z-coordinates (depths) are preserved, not overwritten by GPS depth_reference
- [ ] Unconnected sections maintain position when first datum is set

## References

- Epic spec: `.flow/specs/fn-19-mmx.md`
- Current set_zero_datum: `src-tauri/src/models/project.rs:539-564`
- Section offsets: `src-tauri/src/models/project.rs` (`section_offsets` field)
- Connected groups: `src-tauri/src/models/project.rs:202-222`
- Merge pattern: `src-tauri/src/models/project.rs:333-443`
- Undo data: `src-tauri/src/core/undo.rs:72-77`
- ENU projection: Wikipedia Local_tangent_plane_coordinates

# fn-19-mmx.1 Add GPS-to-local ENU coordinate conversion

## Description
Add GPS-to-local coordinate conversion using ENU (East-North-Up) projection in the Rust backend. This converts WGS84 GPS coordinates to local meters relative to a reference point.

**Size:** S
**Files:** `src-tauri/src/models/project.rs` (or new `src-tauri/src/utils/geo.rs`)

## Approach

Implement inline ENU projection (no external crate dependency):
1. `geodetic_to_ecef(lat, lon, alt)` - Convert geodetic to ECEF
2. `ecef_to_enu(dx, dy, dz, lat0, lon0)` - Convert ECEF difference to ENU
3. `gps_to_local(gps, origin_gps)` - High-level function for datum positioning

Follow WGS84 constants and formulas from Wikipedia Local_tangent_plane_coordinates.

## Key context

WGS84 ellipsoid constants:
- Semi-major axis (a): 6,378,137.0 meters
- Eccentricity squared (e²): 0.00669437999014

ENU result: East→x (meters), North→y (meters), Up→z (ignored for cave surveys)
## Acceptance
- [ ] `geodetic_to_ecef(lat: f64, lon: f64, alt: f64) -> (f64, f64, f64)` implemented
- [ ] `gps_to_local(gps: &GpsCoordinates, origin: &GpsCoordinates) -> (f64, f64)` implemented
- [ ] Uses WGS84 ellipsoid constants
- [ ] Latitude/longitude inputs in degrees (converted to radians internally)
- [ ] Returns (east, north) offset in meters
- [ ] Handles edge cases: same point returns (0, 0)
- [ ] Unit tests for known GPS coordinate pairs
- [ ] Rust tests pass (cargo test)

# fn-19-mmx.2 Enhance set_zero_datum to reposition sections

## Description
Enhance `Project::set_zero_datum()` to reposition the station and all connected sections when a GPS reference is set.

**Size:** M
**Files:** `src-tauri/src/models/project.rs`

## Approach

1. Call `get_connected_section_ids()` to find all affected sections
2. Compute current station position via `compute_station_raw_coords()`
3. For first datum (no existing datums): Station becomes (0,0), adjust all connected section offsets so station lands at origin
4. For subsequent datums: Compute GPS offset from first datum using `gps_to_local()`, apply offset to connected sections
5. Store GPS in `zero_datums` vector
6. Trigger coordinate recomputation

Follow pattern from `merge_stations()` at `project.rs:333-443` for offset application.

## Key context

Section positioning uses `section_offsets: HashMap<SectionId, (f64, f64)>`. When computing station coordinates, these offsets are applied. The goal is to compute offsets such that the datum station ends up at its GPS-derived local position.
## Acceptance
- [ ] First datum station repositions to (0, 0, z)
- [ ] All connected sections move with datum station
- [ ] Subsequent datums positioned at GPS offset from first datum
- [ ] Section offsets updated in `section_offsets` HashMap
- [ ] Existing section offsets respected (adjustment, not replacement)
- [ ] Z-coordinates preserved (not affected by GPS)
- [ ] Detailed logging of GPS coords, computed offsets, affected sections
- [ ] Returns success/error result
- [ ] Rust tests pass (cargo test)

# fn-19-mmx.3 Enhance undo data to capture section_offsets

## Description
Enhance `UndoData::ZeroDatumInfo` to capture `section_offsets` before modification, enabling full undo of repositioning.

**Size:** S
**Files:** `src-tauri/src/core/undo.rs`, `src-tauri/src/models/project.rs`

## Approach

1. Extend `ZeroDatumInfo` struct to include `previous_offsets: HashMap<SectionId, (f64, f64)>`
2. Before setting datum, capture current offsets for all affected sections
3. On undo, restore previous offsets from `ZeroDatumInfo`
4. On redo, reapply the computed offsets

Follow existing undo pattern at `undo.rs:72-77`.

## Key context

Current `ZeroDatumInfo` only stores `previous_gps`. After this task, it must also store the section offsets that existed before the operation, so undo can fully restore the previous state.
## Acceptance
- [ ] `ZeroDatumInfo` includes `previous_offsets: HashMap<SectionId, (f64, f64)>`
- [ ] Section offsets captured before datum set
- [ ] Undo restores previous section offsets
- [ ] Undo restores previous GPS (or removes if new datum)
- [ ] Redo reapplies datum and computed offsets
- [ ] Rust tests pass (cargo test)

# fn-19-mmx.4 Update merge_stations to propagate datum repositioning

## Description
Update `merge_stations()` to propagate datum repositioning when a section without a datum merges into a group that has one.

**Size:** M
**Files:** `src-tauri/src/models/project.rs`

## Approach

1. After merge completes, check if merged group now has a zero datum
2. If yes, recompute offsets for newly connected sections relative to the datum
3. Use same offset calculation logic as `set_zero_datum()`
4. Ensure undo of merge also restores pre-merge offsets

Follow existing merge logic at `project.rs:333-443`.

## Key context

Current merge handles offset calculation to align stations at merge point. After merge, if the combined group has a datum, sections should be positioned relative to that datum. The newly merged section needs its offset adjusted.
## Acceptance
- [ ] Merge into datum group repositions merged sections
- [ ] Merged sections align to datum coordinate system
- [ ] Existing sections in datum group stay in place
- [ ] Undo of merge restores pre-merge positions
- [ ] Works for both directions (A into B, B into A)
- [ ] Rust tests pass (cargo test)

# fn-19-mmx.5 Add validation for duplicate datum in connected group

## Description
Add validation to prevent setting a second zero datum on a station that is in the same connected group as an existing datum.

**Size:** S
**Files:** `src-tauri/src/models/project.rs`

## Approach

1. Before setting datum, call `get_connected_section_ids()` for the target station
2. Check if any station in connected group already has `is_zero_datum: true`
3. If yes, return error: "This station group already has a zero datum at Station X"
4. Allow setting datum if no existing datum in connected group

## Key context

One datum per connected group rule. Disconnected groups can each have their own datum. The validation must traverse merges to find all stations in the group.
## Acceptance
- [ ] Error returned when trying to set duplicate datum in same group
- [ ] Error message identifies existing datum station
- [ ] Disconnected groups can each have their own datum
- [ ] Validation runs before any state changes
- [ ] Rust tests pass (cargo test)

# fn-19-mmx.6 Update frontend to fit-to-bounds after datum set

## Description
Update frontend to call `triggerFitToBounds()` after setting zero datum so the map view shows the repositioned content.

**Size:** S
**Files:** `src/store/projectStore.ts`, `src/App.tsx`

## Approach

1. In `setZeroDatum` action (projectStore.ts:683-689), after successful result, call `triggerFitToBounds()`
2. Or handle in App.tsx where import placement already calls `triggerFitToBounds()`
3. Ensure fit-to-bounds respects any padding/margin settings

Follow existing pattern from import placement at `App.tsx:236-244`.

## Key context

`triggerFitToBounds()` is in `useUIStore`. It triggers the map to zoom/pan to fit all visible content. After datum repositioning, sections may have moved significantly.
## Acceptance
- [ ] Map fits to bounds after successful datum set
- [ ] Fit-to-bounds called only on success (not on error)
- [ ] Works for both setting new datum and modifying existing
- [ ] TypeScript types pass (pnpm tsc --noEmit)
